chunks.content: 96 One Thing You Shouldn’t Skip in Your Diligence Checklist Hi Sara, What if I told you skipping one simple step in your diligence checklist could cause you to lose your business—Too dramatic? How about missing this one thing that could cause you to go bankrupt? The world to end! - How’s that for drama? In my role as a deal attorney, I am pretty much just a perpetual buzzkill when it comes to cutting corners in business deals. Yesterday, someone asked me if they could delete a certain section from their diligence checklist because it didn’t seem relevant. I get it, it’s usually in the first few lines of the list and those lists are long. As a human person and business person, I empathize a great deal with people wanting to cut down a very very long list of things to do, but unfortunately you really really should do it. Spoiler alert: it’s very relevant. The Diligence Detail You Can’t Overlook At the top of every diligence checklist is something that sounds boring but is absolutely critical: Articles of Organization, Incorporation, and Organizational Documents. Why does this matter? As many people have asked me, “Why do I need this if this is an asset purchase?” Because these documents tell you who owns the business and what its assets are. If you don’t verify ownership, you could end up in a nightmare scenario where: The seller isn’t actually the owner (GASP) You paid for assets that legally belong to someone else (LOUDER GASP) And guess what? Whether it’s a stock or an asset purchase, that’s your problem to untangle after the deal closes. Don’t Take the Seller’s Word for It Even in an asset purchase—where you’re buying the stuff, not the company itself—you need to know who legally owns the assets you think you’re buying. These documents give you that clarity. Skipping them is a big risk and you probably don’t like taking risks. Let this be your friendly reminder: keep those organizational documents on your checklist. They might be “boring,” but they’ll save you from a world of hurt later. Need help making sure you’re keeping your deal on track?
